summary.title: Project R: Build Your Own Regular Expression Engines
summary.one_liner: You learn to build your own regex engine in Python, covering parsing, backtracking, NFA, and DFA approaches across four graded parts.
takeaways: Regex parsing can be done in roughly 100 lines of Python.
A backtracking regex executor can be written in roughly 50 lines.
An NFA-based regex engine is covered for intermediate readers, in roughly 100 lines of Python.
The series is split into four parts: R1 parsing (beginner), R2 backtracking (beginner), R3 graph traversal and NFA (intermediate), R4 DFA (advanced).
summary.summary: This page is the introduction to Project R, a series of tutorials on building regular expression engines in Python. It states that regex can be understood by building one or two engines yourself. The series is organized into four parts: parsing regular expressions, regex via backtracking, graph traversal and regex (NFA), and deterministic finite automata (DFA), with difficulty levels from beginner to advanced. The page gives approximate code sizes for each approach but the detailed material is in the linked parts.
